newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips drive up Morocco bourse weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips drive up Morocco bourse weekly trade.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended the week on Friday higher driven by blue chips companies, including the largest market capitalisation ONA Group, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 429.43 points, up from 414.34 points a week earlier.
"The market continues its upward trend as it appreciated by 4.03 percent compared with a traded volume of 222 million dirhams," said Mouna Lahlou, analyst at Casablanca Finance Intermediation.
ONA Group was among the blue chips that drove the market higher, she said.
A block of 65,800 shares of ONA exchanged hands during the week, she added.

ONA, which holds stakes in more than 100 companies, gained 48 dirhams in one week to close at 450 dirhams on Friday compared with the previous week. The group has market capitalisation of 7.7 billion dirhams.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant, rose two dirhams to close at 247 dirhams. "A block of 71,255 shares of Samir were exchanged during the week," CFI said.
Wafabank, one the main market capitalisations, rose 10 dirhams to close at 503 compared with last Friday.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the bourse's largest capitalisation, rose 5.71 percent to close at 740 dirhams, analysts said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which has interests in more than 40 companies, closed at 590 dirhams, up 15 dirhams on the previous week.
A Casablanca-based stockbroker said the market also reacted to the announcement of the expected floation on the bourse of FERTIMA fertiliser company.
An official at the privatisation ministry said 30 percent of FERTIMA's stock worth 120 million dirhams will be sold to general public next month.
Casablanca Finance Group Index, which tracks the 25 most liquid stocks, broke a fourth consecutive record high this week, Lahlou added
The bourse volume jumped to 222 million dirhams from 160 million dirhams a week earlier, stockbrokers said.
